config.description: read-only PCIe investigation on the secondary GPU server (GA-B250-HD3P-CF, BIOS F8): lspci LnkCap/LnkSta/LnkSta2 + AER on both ends, nvidia-smi link state at idle and under the live 27B workload, sysfs, 128 MiB cuMemcpy x12; single continuous host boot since 2026-11-14 (the dual-3060 installation). No register writes, no resets, no rebinds.

workload.fixture: 128MiB cuMemcpy; nvidia-smi under the live 27B endpoint load

metrics.name: chipset_card_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: RTX 3060 (EVGA PX1) on the chipset PCIEX4_1 slot (PCH port 00:1d.0, LnkCap x4): negotiated Gen3 x1 at idle and under load; the same port verified Gen3 x4 on 2026-08-17/09-06 with the previous card (GTX 1050, via ribbon riser) in it. The card itself has no x4 record; the 'x4 era' wording in the November reports is retracted.

metrics.name: chipset_card_h2d_gbps
metrics.definition: median of 12 128 MiB cuMemcpy host-to-device (x1 Gen3 ceiling)

metrics.name: cpu_slot_card_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: RTX 3060 LHR on the CPU x16 slot: Gen3 x16; 8.446/8.110 GB/s H2D/D2H

metrics.name: gtx1050_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: moved to an x1 slot (PCH 00:1c.6, DMI J8B4, LnkCap x1) during the 2026-11-14 installation; Gen3 x1 = slot-limited, not degraded (it did x4 in PCIEX4_1 in Aug/Sep)

metrics.name: gt1030_negotiated_width
metrics.definition: on the second chipset x4 slot (00:1b.0), unchanged since August

metrics.name: aer_errors
metrics.definition: corrected and uncorrected AER counters clean on the chipset card; a stable x1 link can train without errors, so this does not prove the link intended x4

notes: open question (case A vs B): the manual limits PCIEX4_1 to x1 only when the PCIEX1_2 x1 slot is populated, but the owner's installation photo shows the riser in the upper x1 (PCIEX1_1), which has no documented sharing rule. If the riser is actually in PCIEX1_2 the x1 is by design; otherwise it is a physical signal/seating issue. Onsite check only.
